objective: Build the missing robot structural layer from actuator output loads through free-body diagrams, stress/strain, section mechanics, combined loading, local stability, bolted joints, mission fatigue, modes, FEA evidence, thermal mechanics and physical correlation; then reconstruct NASA's 2025 preloaded-bolt report and Manson et al.'s 1967 double-linear fatigue note as separate source-bound articles.

request_interpretation.curriculum_intent: Replace the actuator article's lumped link/housing stiffness with the physical load paths, geometry, material response, failure modes and evidence needed before controller claims can be trusted.
request_interpretation.depth_intent: Write a private forty-six-premise shoulder-joint transfer failure and require the public bundle to make every premise diagnosable without publishing the scenario as a quiz.
request_interpretation.source_intent: Read primary artifacts completely before reconstruction, preserve page-level author intent and admitted limits, and keep historical fatigue evidence separate from current fastener research and transferable mechanics.
request_interpretation.formula_intent: Give every display equation Korean operation annotations and exactly one adjacent FormulaNote; split long equations by semantic operation instead of using horizontal scroll or unreadable scaling.
request_interpretation.visual_intent: Use eleven mechanism-specific causal labs whose controls change loads, stresses, deformation, margin, clamp state, damage, modes, convergence, thermal drift or evidence acceptance rather than merely changing color.
request_interpretation.small_model_intent: Persist source slices, premise assignments, derivation order, Viz contracts, rejected sources, browser defects and repairs so 4B and 9B models can replay bounded passes.

existing_coverage: robot-actuator-mechanics converts motor output into joint torque, inertia, compliance, bearing load and brake handover
robot-dynamics-feedback-control models feedback around an abstract plant
signals, systems, vectors, calculus and probability articles provide mathematical prerequisites
missing_chain: pose/event to load-case ledger, coordinate frame and free-body diagram
force and moment transport to local section resultants
stress, strain, modulus, strength and displacement as distinct quantities
area, second moment, bending, torsion and combined-stress reasoning
notch, allowable, buckling, contact and failure-mode-specific margins
preload, clamp, slip, separation, load introduction and thermal bolt load
mission history, rainflow, mean/amplitude, S-N boundary and order effects
structural modes, damping, excitation and controller interaction
FEA boundary/contact/mesh diagnostics and non-singular quantities of interest
thermal resistance, expansion, constraint stress, alignment and preload drift
physical correlation through reaction, strain, displacement, modal, thermal and preload measurements

scope_split.concept: Transferable robot structural mechanics and the complete model-to-test evidence chain.
scope_split.current_report: NASA/TM-20250005284 preserves the stiffness-based load-introduction derivation, FEA/test comparisons and unconservative boundary.
scope_split.foundational_paper: NASA TN D-3839 preserves the Miner baseline failure, double-linear proposal, experimental revision and smooth-specimen boundary.
scope_split.deferred: Fracture mechanics/damage tolerance and composite structures require dedicated next layers rather than shallow add-on paragraphs.

private_transfer_gate.scenario: A gravity-loaded shoulder link passes a peak von-Mises screenshot while its team mixes load planes, omits offset moments and emergency braking, confuses strength with stiffness, double-counts Kt, ignores buckling/contact/preload scatter and separation, reduces the mission to one peak, uses Miner as a universal law, accepts a singular FEA maximum, ignores thermal gradients and closes the claim without synchronized physical evidence.

coverage_groups.public_resolution: Load-case ledger, FBD, wrench transport and Load Path Lab.
Stress-strain-displacement chain, material boundary and Stress-Strain Lab.
Section geometry, bending, deflection, torsion and combined-stress labs.
Notch, source-bound allowable, margin and buckling gates.
Bolt stiffness share, load introduction, clamp/slip/separation and NASA source spine.
Cycle decomposition, rainflow, Miner boundary, load order and Manson source spine.
Mode, damping, excitation and controller-separation reasoning.
FEA equilibrium, singularity, convergence, contact and analytical bracket gates.
Thermal compatibility and multi-channel physical correlation closure.

private_transfer_gate.publication_policy: The compound problem remains private. The public prose, formulas, controls, failure states and source boundaries supply the insight needed to solve it.

source_decisions.boundary: A design manual supplies mechanics and process cautions; current program standards and exact allowables still govern qualification.

source_decisions.source: John K. Ramsey, Mechanics of Preloaded Bolt Tensile Loading With Focus on Load Introduction Factor
source_decisions.identity: NASA/TM-20250005284, May 2025, 112 PDF pages including Appendices A-J
source_decisions.boundary: SBLIF can be closer than GLIF but can also be unconservative when path stiffness is approximated poorly; the report is not a universal standard.

source_decisions.source: S. S. Manson, J. C. Freche and C. R. Ensign, Application of a Double Linear Damage Rule to Cumulative Fatigue
source_decisions.identity: NASA TN D-3839, April 1967, 41 PDF pages
source_decisions.boundary: Evidence comes from limited smooth 1/4-inch specimens and two-level histories; coefficients and literal crack-stage language do not transfer directly to robot structures.

source_decisions.source: NBS Special Publication 702, Fatigue and Fracture
used_for: fatigue, S-N, mean and alternating stress vocabulary
source_decisions.boundary: Vocabulary does not replace detail-specific modern fatigue or fracture qualification.

rejected_source_decisions.source: M. A. Miner, Cumulative Damage in Fatigue, 1945
rejected_source_decisions.reason: The publisher PDF was inaccessible in this run and no fully auditable open primary copy was available. The result was not promoted to a standalone reconstruction merely from secondary summaries.
rejected_source_decisions.replacement: Manson et al. 1967 was fully downloaded and read; it states the Miner baseline, demonstrates its order limitation, proposes an alternative and records the authors' own revision.

local_documents.status: read candidate, not selected for a standalone spine in this milestone

source_extraction.full_read_claim: All 112 pages of the selected NASA report, including Appendices A-J, and all 41 pages of the selected Manson note, including appendices, were included in the reconstruction pass.

events.observed: The actuator curriculum ended with lumped housing/link stiffness and the feedback curriculum began with an assumed plant.
events.inference: A reader could calculate motor torque yet could not prove where the load travels, what fails, or which physical measurement falsifies the structural model.
events.decision: Insert a structural mechanics layer before deeper fracture/composite and controller integration.
events.verification: Eleven sections now form a load-case-to-physical-correlation chain and the learning graph links actuator, current report and foundational paper.

events.observed: A single peak stress screenshot can pass while forty-six independent assumptions about loads, joints, fatigue, dynamics, thermal state and evidence are false.
events.inference: A chapter outline alone would miss implementation-depth failure paths.
events.decision: Use the private forty-six-premise shoulder problem as the authoring coverage gate.
events.verification: The spec maps each premise group to prose, equation, causal lab, evidence state or source boundary.

events.observed: Current bolt research, a historical fatigue model and general mechanics carry different evidence and transfer limits.
events.inference: Combining them into one narrative would make report-specific approximations look like universal laws.
events.decision: Keep one transferable concept article and two source-bound reconstruction articles.
events.verification: NASA exposes seven evidence states and six formulas; Manson exposes seven evidence states and six formulas, each with author intent and limits.

events.observed: The original 1945 Miner publisher PDF returned access denial.
events.inference: A standalone reconstruction would violate the full-source reading policy.
events.decision: Do not fabricate a Miner article from recollection; use the fully readable Manson primary source and keep Miner as a bounded baseline.
events.verification: No Miner standalone metadata or page exists; the source decision is explicit in the run record.

events.observed: Generic cards and straight arrows cannot expose cross products, section geometry, clamp loss, fatigue order, mode crossing, FEA convergence or thermal compatibility.
events.inference: A color-only restyle would not improve comprehension.
events.decision: Use eleven distinct observables and require every control to change a computed conclusion or model state.
events.verification: Browser QA changed all eleven labs; screenshot review found no clipping or internal scroll at 360 and 1440 pixels.

events.observed: The first run measured 0.72 at 360 pixels and 0.79 at 390 pixels for a one-line mean/amplitude equation; the moment-transport equation also reached 0.79.
events.inference: The formulas fit technically but the operations and annotations were too compressed to read comfortably.
events.decision: Split mean and alternating stress into aligned semantic rows and shorten moment labels without removing the physical terms.
events.verification: The concept article passed the 0.82/0.86 acceptance floors and public measurements became 0.83/0.92.

events.observed: A Manson intersection formula passed alone at 0.86 but dipped to 0.81 during two-worker regression under font-load timing.
events.inference: A boundary-value pass was not robust enough for production.
events.decision: Shorten the Korean annotations to 단계 전환점, 실험선 교점, 작은 수명비 and 큰 수명비.
events.verification: All four Manson viewport tests and the subsequent full connected regression passed.

events.observed: Local build success does not prove that the public reverse-proxied asset graph changed.
events.inference: Completion requires service restart, route checks and browser QA against the public host.
events.decision: Restart cm-blog.service and rerun the complete structural suite at the public domain.
events.verification: Service is active, all three routes return HTTP 200 and public Playwright passed 17/17 in 30.4 seconds.

small_model_replay.repair_protocol: Return viewport, article slug, selector or math source, expected invariant, observed metric, screenshot, source boundary and allowed files. A repair model may split formulas, shorten labels or recompose layout but may not weaken a scientific claim, remove a failure boundary or lower the acceptance floor.
